parts.name: yard_board
parts.notes: Hexagonal slab, 230mm corner-to-corner (idea.json's stated figure, used directly as the x bbox extent), 12mm thick, chamfered skirt. bbox y=200mm is MY computation from the stated 230mm corner-to-corner figure via standard hexagon geometry (flat-to-flat width = corner-to-corner x sqrt(3)/2 = 230 x 0.866 = 199.2mm, rounded to 200mm) — idea.json only states the one diagonal, not the perpendicular width (see unstated_in_spec). bbox z=42mm = 12mm slab + 30mm pin height, a straight sum of two numbers idea.json states separately and never combines (see unstated_in_spec). 37 integral pins on a triangular lattice at 30mm spacing (centre, ring of 6, ring of 12, ring of 18 = 1+6+12+18=37), each pin 8mm diameter x 30mm tall, standing proud of the floor. OWNS the pin diameter (8mm), pin height (30mm) and pin spacing (30mm, exactly matching every gear's 30mm pitch-circle diameter so adjacent pins mesh) — every gear/millstone/crank bore and every meshing check derives from these three numbers, never restates them. The 18 outer-ring pins each sit inside a 1.2mm raised sill marking them as the only pins a mill_gear or crank_gear may stand on; the other 19 pins (centre + inner ring of 6 + ring of 12) take supply gears only and carry no sill. Floor between pins carries 1mm raised plank ribs — the shallower of the board's two relief features (1.2mm sills vs 1mm ribs), so 1.0mm is the binding value reported in relief_mm. No `recesses` block: pins are posts a bore rides over, not pockets a piece drops into, so this is captured entirely through the `joins` interfaces below rather than the ergonomics_check `recesses` formula (mirrors armillary's axle-post/disc-bore precedent, which also carried no matching `recesses` entry). Single tile — 230x200x42mm is well inside the 246x246x251mm P2S bed.

parts.name: gear_low
parts.notes: Low-tier gear: 12 teeth on a 30mm pitch circle, ~35mm outside diameter (idea.json's stated figure, used directly as bbox x/y). Teeth band occupies the lower half of the pin height, starting just above the floor, ~10mm face — read as the piece's own full standalone body height (bbox z=10mm): a squat toothed puck, not a taller piece with empty space above it. 8.6mm bore (idea.json's own explicit figure), three round lightening holes in the web (functional grip cuts, not a surface-relief motif, so no relief_mm declared). Rests flat, toothed face down or up, axis vertical — this is the SAME orientation the piece takes on a pin, so its table-resting bbox and its mounted bbox are identical. Only engages the LOWER 10mm of a 30mm pin; the remaining 20mm of pin material is exposed above it when placed, and is the segment a neighbouring gear_high's teeth mesh at (see the yard_board joins interface).

parts.name: gear_high
parts.notes: High-tier gear: same 12-tooth, 30mm-pitch, ~35mm-OD ring as gear_low, carried at the TOP of a plain smooth column so the teeth occupy the upper part of the pin height and bare shaft fills the rest below, down to the floor. Total standalone height = 30mm, matching yard_board's full 30mm pin height exactly (so the piece fully houses its pin with no stub exposed, unlike gear_low) — idea.json describes this qualitatively ('teeth occupy the UPPER half... nothing but bare shaft below') without a combined total-height figure, so 30mm is my reading of 'spans the pin' taken literally (see unstated_in_spec). Column diameter is UNSTATED in idea.json ('a plain smooth column' with no number); I set it to 16mm — enough wall around the shared 8.6mm bore to print soundly while reading visibly narrower than the 35mm tooth ring, matching the 'lamppost' silhouette idea.json's own part_vocabulary calls for. Same 8.6mm bore and clearance as gear_low (idea.json states this explicitly: 'Same bore and clearance').

parts.name: gear_tandem
parts.notes: Full-height gear: the same 12-tooth/30mm-pitch/35mm-OD tooth profile run the whole pin height as one barrel, ~28mm face. I reconciled idea.json's two figures for this piece — 'the whole pin height' (30mm, from yard_board's own pin spec) and '~28mm face' — by reading the overall body as 30mm tall (fully housing the pin, no stub, matching 'full-height' literally) with 28mm of that being the actual tooth-cut face and a 1mm untoothed lead-in rim top and bottom (30-2=28); I did not pick one figure and discard the other (see unstated_in_spec). 8.6mm bore, inherited uniformly from gear_low's stated figure since idea.json gives this piece no separate bore number (see unstated_in_spec). The only supply piece whose bore is engaged over the FULL pin depth AND whose teeth are cut the full height, so it is the only supply piece that can mesh with a low-tier piece at the bottom of one neighbouring pin and a high-tier piece at the top of another simultaneously.

parts.name: mill_gear_tri
parts.notes: Millstone, three-sided hub. Full-height tooth barrel identical to gear_tandem's (30mm tall, 35mm OD, 8.6mm bore inherited the same way — see gear_tandem's notes), crowned by a dressed grinding disc cut with 1.2mm-deep radial furrows (idea.json's stated relief figure, used directly as relief_mm). Crown and hub dimensions are UNSTATED beyond qualitative description ('the crown does not overhang the tooth circle'; hub 'rises... as a finger grip'): I set the crown to 34mm diameter (1mm inside the 35mm tooth OD, satisfying the 'does not overhang' constraint) x 6mm thick (enough material to carve a 1.2mm furrow pattern with wall left over), and a triangular prism hub ~16mm across flats x 12mm tall above that, for a total standalone height of 30+6+12=48mm (see unstated_in_spec). Told apart from the other three millstones by hub flat-count alone (3 flats), per idea.json's part_vocabulary — identical bbox, crown and barrel to mill_gear_square/penta/hex.

parts.name: mill_gear_square
parts.notes: Millstone, four-sided hub. Identical barrel, crown and overall dimensions to mill_gear_tri (see its notes for the crown/hub sizing rationale) — only the hub's flat count differs (4 flats).

parts.name: mill_gear_penta
parts.notes: Millstone, five-sided hub. Identical barrel, crown and overall dimensions to mill_gear_tri (see its notes) — only the hub's flat count differs (5 flats).

parts.name: mill_gear_hex
parts.notes: Millstone, six-sided hub. Identical barrel, crown and overall dimensions to mill_gear_tri (see its notes) — only the hub's flat count differs (6 flats).

parts.name: crank_gear
parts.notes: The only power piece: a full-height tooth barrel (30mm tall, 35mm OD, 8.6mm bore — same reasoning as gear_tandem's barrel, see its notes) topped by a solid cap carrying an offset arm and a 14mm-diameter knurled knob standing 22mm proud (both figures idea.json states explicitly), plus a 1.2mm raised direction arrow (idea.json's stated relief figure, used directly as relief_mm). Cap thickness (3mm), arm length (knob-centre 21mm from the gear axis) and arm cross-section are UNSTATED in idea.json, which gives only the knob's own size — I sized the arm to clear the 35mm barrel body, giving a standalone bbox of 46 x 35 x 55mm (barrel 30 + cap 3 + knob 22 = 55mm tall; footprint = 17.5mm barrel radius on one side + 21mm arm + 7mm knob radius = 28mm on the other side, rounded to 46mm total x-span) (see unstated_in_spec). GENUINE UNRESOLVED TENSION, flagged rather than silently resolved: idea.json's own rule has the crank relocate to any empty yard pin every round on a 30mm-pitch grid; an offset arm long enough to grip comfortably puts the knob's outer edge close to where a neighbouring yard pin's own piece would stand, so some crank placements may crowd or foul whatever occupies the adjacent yard pin. I did not invent a rule to resolve this (e.g. a keep-clear zone) since idea.json states none; the builder should route the arm as a solid gusset from the barrel wall up to the knob base (not a thin free bar) so it self-supports in print, per print_plan.

parts.name: grain_pellet
parts.notes: Score piece: 15mm-diameter, 5mm-thick domed washer with a 9mm hole (all three figures idea.json states explicitly). Smooth and untoothed by design so it can never be mistaken for a gear — no relief_mm declared, since idea.json states no surface motif for it.

parts.name: sack_spindle
parts.notes: Score post, one per player. 40mm round base (idea.json's stated figure) with a 1mm chevron texture on its skirt (idea.json's stated relief figure, used directly as relief_mm), and an 8.5mm rod standing 62mm tall (idea.json's stated figures). Base HEIGHT is UNSTATED — idea.json gives only the base diameter — I set it to 8mm for structural stability under a loaded rod, giving a total standalone height of 8+62=70mm (see unstated_in_spec). idea.json's own capacity claim ('capacity 12 grain_pellet with room to lift the top one off with a thumbnail') checks out arithmetically against the stated numbers without any invention: 12 x 5mm pellet thickness = 60mm, leaving exactly 2mm of the stated 62mm rod clear above a full stack for a thumbnail pinch.

parts.name: granary_bin
parts.notes: Open bin, 70 x 50 x 25mm (idea.json's stated figures, used directly), thumb scallop cut into one long wall, 1mm chevron relief on the front (idea.json's stated relief figure, used directly as relief_mm). Deliberately carries no `recesses` block: idea.json calls this an 'open bin' holding the loose grain_pellet supply, not a fitted pocket sized to one piece, so the ergonomics_check seat-clearance formula does not apply here (mirrors yard_board's supply pile of loose gears, and armillary's reserve_column precedent for bulk/loose storage that isn't a per-piece seat).

interfaces.joint: post-through-bore, rotating/liftable slip fit, partial engagement
interfaces.notes: gear_low's 8.6mm bore rides yard_board's 8mm pin, engaging only the piece's own 10mm body height out of the pin's 30mm total — the pin's remaining 20mm stands exposed above a seated gear_low (this is the zone a neighbouring gear_high's teeth occupy for the mesh to make sense). Clearance = (8.6-8)/2 = 0.3mm per side. yard_board OWNS the 8mm pin diameter; gear_low's bore derives its clearance from it, not restated independently for the other bore-bearing pieces below.

interfaces.joint: post-through-bore, rotating/liftable slip fit, full engagement
interfaces.notes: Representative for every full-height piece — gear_high, gear_tandem, mill_gear_tri/square/penta/hex, and crank_gear — all of which share the same 8.6mm bore engaging the pin's entire 30mm length with no stub exposed. Same 0.3mm-per-side clearance as gear_low's partial-engagement fit above, derived from the same yard_board-owned 8mm pin diameter. FLAGGED TOLERANCE: 0.3mm/side is tighter than this pipeline's usual 0.4mm minimum seat clearance, but it is idea.json's own explicit figure (8.6mm bore stated directly, not approximated) set against yard_board's own explicit 8mm pin — idea.json's prose elsewhere calls this a 'generous 0.5mm running clearance,' which does not quite match its own 8.6mm/8mm arithmetic (0.3mm/side, or 0.6mm on the diameter). I kept the more specific, numeric figures (8.6mm and 8mm) rather than loosening either to match the looser prose descriptor, and am flagging the mismatch rather than silently resolving it. Every gear here must lift off and relocate every round (SHIFT, crank relocation), so this is functionally a repeated-use slip joint, not a one-time press fit — a build that comes out tighter than 0.3mm/side in practice should be treated as a print-tolerance failure, not a spec ambiguity.

interfaces.joint: tooth-to-tooth gear mesh across adjacent yard-board pins
interfaces.notes: Representative for all tooth-height-matched meshing: gear_low meshes with gear_low, gear_high meshes with gear_high, and any full-height piece (gear_tandem, all four mill_gear variants, crank_gear) meshes with anything on a neighbouring pin regardless of tier. This is the mechanism the whole game runs on. All pieces share one 12-tooth, 30mm-pitch-circle, ~35mm-OD profile, and yard_board's own 30mm pin spacing exactly equals that pitch-circle diameter, so two meshing pieces on adjacent pins engage correctly by construction — this is why yard_board OWNS the 30mm pin spacing and no gear restates it. Backlash is UNSTATED as a number in idea.json ('generous backlash so a long train turns freely by hand'); I set it to 0.4mm total (0.2mm per flank), a workable FDM gear-mesh backlash figure, so a long train of gear_low pieces turns freely by hand as idea.json's own text requires (see unstated_in_spec).

grain_pellet's 9mm hole rides sack_spindle's 8.5mm rod (both idea.json's own stated figures) — clearance (9-8.5)/2 = 0.25mm per side. FLAGGED TOLERANCE, same reasoning as the gear/pin joins above: tighter than the pipeline's usual 0.4mm minimum, but both numbers are idea.json's own explicit figures, kept as stated rather than loosened.

Up to 12 grain_pellet stack on one sack_spindle rod (idea.json's stated capacity, confirmed arithmetically in sack_spindle's own notes: 12 x 5mm = 60mm against a 62mm rod). The stack cannot topple regardless of aspect ratio because the 8.5mm rod running through every pellet's 9mm hole acts as an internal spine, laterally confining the whole stack to the spindle's 40mm base footprint — the toppling check this interface kind implies is satisfied by the rod's confinement, not by the stack's own bulk.

print_plan.notes:
No part exceeds the 246 x 246 x 251mm P2S bed — yard_board (230x200x42mm) is the largest footprint and prints as a single tile, no dovetail joins needed anywhere in this brief. yard_board prints flat, floor-down: all 37 pins are plain vertical cylinders standing up from the top face, and both the 1.2mm sills and 1mm plank ribs are top-face reliefs — no supports. gear_low prints flat, axis vertical (its natural resting orientation, identical to its mounted orientation on a pin) — a simple toothed puck with chamfered tooth crowns, no supports. gear_high prints axis vertical, smooth-column end down, tooth ring at the top — a straight extrusion with radial teeth at the top, standard FDM gear-printing orientation, no supports. gear_tandem, mill_gear_tri/square/penta/hex and crank_gear all print axis vertical, barrel-bottom down, for the same reason — teeth and crown/hub features build straight up in flat top-face layers, no supports needed for any of them except the detail below. crank_gear's offset arm needs deliberate routing: model it as a solid triangular gusset running from the barrel's outer wall up to the knob's base, not as a thin free-floating bar — a gusset self-supports as it builds; a free bar bridging to an isolated knob would need support material mid-print. grain_pellet prints flat, domed face up or down, no supports. sack_spindle prints base-down, rod standing straight up (self-supporting on a 40mm base) with 1mm chevron relief on the skirt as a straightforward vertical-wall texture, no supports. granary_bin prints flat, open-top, thumb scallop as a simple wall cutout, no supports.

blocks.py notes for the builder: add_piece_family for every multi-copy family here — 14x gear_low, 7x gear_high, 3x gear_tandem, 28x grain_pellet, and the 4x sack_spindle — each copy must land as a separately named assembly child, per the lesson graduated from the 48-tile/65-piece union failure; nothing in this brief should ever be unioned into one body. shared_positions (or an equivalent hand-rolled generator) should produce yard_board's 37-point triangular lattice (centre + ring of 6 + ring of 12 + ring of 18 at 30mm spacing) exactly once, reused for cutting/marking the pins themselves, the 18 sill rings, and the plank-rib layout between them — never regenerate that lattice's trig a second time. seated_pair is not a direct fit here (its default free-fit formula is for a press-fit pocket, not a repeatedly-lifted rotating bore-over-post), but its underlying discipline — one part OWNS a dimension, the mating part's clearance is always derived, never a second independent number — is exactly how every bore in this brief is written: yard_board owns the 8mm pin diameter and 30mm pin spacing; every gear, millstone and the crank derive their 8.6mm bore and their mesh geometry from those two numbers alone.

unstated_in_spec: yard_board's second footprint dimension (the hexagon's flat-to-flat width, ~200mm) is my computation from idea.json's stated corner-to-corner figure (230mm) via standard hexagon geometry (230 x sqrt(3)/2 = 199.2mm, rounded to 200mm) — idea.json states only the one diagonal.
yard_board's total standalone height (42mm) is a straight sum of two numbers idea.json states separately and never combines: the 12mm slab and the 30mm pin height.

gear_high's total standalone height (30mm) reads idea.json's qualitative description ('teeth occupy the UPPER half of the pin height... bare shaft below') as spanning the full 30mm pin with no stub exposed, since no combined total-height figure is given directly.

gear_high's smooth column diameter (16mm) is entirely unstated — idea.json says only 'a plain smooth column' with no number. I chose a diameter that leaves printable wall thickness around the shared 8.6mm bore while reading narrower than the 35mm tooth ring, per the 'lamppost' silhouette idea.json's own art direction calls for.

gear_tandem's (and, by the same reasoning, mill_gear_*'s and crank_gear's) total barrel height (30mm) reconciles two numbers idea.json gives for the same piece — 'the whole pin height' (30mm) and '~28mm face' — by treating the body as 30mm tall with 28mm of actual tooth-cut face and a 1mm untoothed lead-in rim top and bottom, rather than picking one figure and silently discarding the other.

gear_tandem's, mill_gear_*'s and crank_gear's 8.6mm bore is inherited from gear_low's explicitly stated figure ('same bore and clearance' is stated only between gear_low and gear_high); idea.json gives no separate bore number for the other full-height pieces, so I extended the one stated figure uniformly across the whole bore-bearing family.

The bore-to-pin clearance (0.3mm per side, from the explicit 8.6mm bore over the explicit 8mm pin) is tighter than idea.json's own prose descriptor elsewhere ('a generous 0.5mm running clearance'). I kept the more specific numeric figures rather than loosening either one to match the looser prose, and flagged the internal inconsistency in the interfaces block instead of silently resolving it.

mill_gear_*'s grinding-disc crown (34mm diameter x 6mm thick) and prism hub (~16mm across flats x 12mm tall) have no stated dimensions in idea.json beyond qualitative description ('does not overhang the tooth circle'; hub 'rises... as a finger grip'). I invented both to give a printable, graspable, furrow-carvable crown and a countable-flats hub.

crank_gear's cap thickness (3mm) and arm geometry (knob-centre 21mm from the gear axis, routed as a solid gusset) are unstated — idea.json gives only the knob's own size (14mm diameter, 22mm proud). I also flagged, without inventing a game-rule fix for it, a genuine geometric tension idea.json's own rules create: a graspable offset arm on a 30mm pin grid can crowd whatever stands on the pin next to wherever the crank relocates.
sack_spindle's base height (8mm) is unstated — idea.json gives only the base diameter (40mm). I sized it for structural stability under a loaded 60mm pellet stack.

Gear-tooth meshing backlash (set to 0.4mm total, 0.2mm per flank) has no stated number anywhere in idea.json, which only describes it qualitatively ('generous backlash so a long train turns freely by hand').
